findings: ImgDecoder blends two feature images using alpha/disparity exponential weights and a learned U-Net; output sigmoid RGB. No hashing/index/search or identity certificate. Exponential weights lack explicit finite/overflow handling.

ResUNet accepts encoder names18/34/50/101/152, but always builds BasicBlock layers[3,4,6,3] through layer3. Filters switch to bottleneck-sized channels for50/101/152 without changing blocks, so advertised alternatives are not implemented consistently. Default resnet34 path not implicated by this static finding.

ResUNet BatchNorm disables running statistics, so eval retains per-input statistics. Inpainting partial convolution explicitly propagates support masks and fills zero-support outputs with zero; generated pixels remain synthesis rather than evidence of source equality.

Depth inpainting forward unconditionally copies input/mask to CPU NumPy into unused visualization variables. This can add synchronization/copy overhead; not benchmarked. Edge forward_3P divides by disp.max without zero guard.

DPT runner strips image extension before write_depth, whose writer always appends .png. Demo get_input_data seeks disparity using original basename extension; ordinary JPG inputs therefore seek a different path. Shared PNG/JPG stems can also overwrite outputs. Static producer-consumer trace plus intercepted writer control, no end-to-end demo.

Original write_pfm grayscale float32 roundtrip succeeds; color float32 branch passes a string to binary write because only else header is encoded, reproducing TypeError. Active depth path is grayscale; no claim this breaks ordinary depth generation.

Original write_depth emits all-zero uint16 PNG values for constant depth in controlled writer interception. It independently normalizes nonconstant images, so depth PNG bytes do not certify original image identity.
DPT requirements pin Torch1.8.1/torchvision0.9.1, differing from root historical environment Torch1.7.1. setup declares only unpinned timm. No combined installation/runtime qualification.
